intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Join locals for picnics beneath thousands of blooming sakura trees, enjoy street food stalls selling yakitori and dango, and soak in the festive atmosphere. The park is especially magical when lanterns illuminate the blossoms at night.

experiences.name: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse your family in a world-class interactive digital art experience where light, sound, and motion blend into breathtaking installations. Children and adults alike are captivated by the ever-changing projections and interactive exhibits. This is one of Japan's most unique and memorable family-friendly cultural attractions.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Japan's most iconic food market and indulge in fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (Japanese omelette), grilled scallops, and matcha treats. Walk through bustling stalls with your family, interact with vendors, and taste your way through authentic Japanese street food culture. A guided tour can enhance the experience with historical and culinary context.

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the iconic towering bamboo forest in Arashiyama, then hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids will love feeding the monkeys from inside a viewing hut while enjoying panoramic views of Kyoto. Combine with a rickshaw ride through the scenic riverside area for a full cultural and nature experience.

experiences.name: Traditional Tea Ceremony and Kimono Experience
experiences.description: Dress your family in beautiful traditional kimonos and participate in an authentic Japanese tea ceremony led by a tea master. Learn the art of matcha preparation, the philosophy of wabi-sabi, and the etiquette of Japanese hospitality. Many studios in Higashiyama offer family-friendly sessions followed by a stroll through historic stone-paved streets lined with cherry blossoms.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and take the airport limousine bus or train to your accommodation (Aegean Bliss Resort). Convenience stores like 7-Eleven or FamilyMart near the station are perfect for grabbing a late-night snack and essentials. Check in and rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Late-night convenience store meal (onigiri, sandwiches, cup noodles) — budget approx ¥500–¥800

day_by_day.notes: Keep your JR Pass (if purchased) ready to activate. Download Google Maps offline for Japan and install a translation app like Google Translate. Exchange some yen at the airport for small expenses. Keep energy levels in mind — tomorrow starts early!

day_by_day.morning: After a good rest, head to a nearby local neighborhood to explore on foot. Visit a local shrine or temple within walking/transit distance of your hotel to ease into Japanese culture. Pick up a classic Japanese breakfast at a nearby bakery or convenience store.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take public transit to a local market or covered shopping arcade (shotengai). Browse budget-friendly souvenirs, try street snacks, and get oriented with the local transit system. Look for 100-yen shops like Daiso for affordable keepsakes.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along a nearby waterfront or park area as the sun sets. Have dinner at a local gyudon (beef bowl) chain like Yoshinoya or Sukiya — filling, fast, and very affordable for the whole family.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast — onigiri, tamagoyaki, and green tea (¥400–¥600)
meals.lunch: Market street food — takoyaki, yakitori, or taiyaki (¥600–¥1,000 per person)
meals.dinner: Yoshinoya or Sukiya gyudon set meal (¥500–¥800 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to recover from jet lag. Keep activities light and nearby. Purchase an IC card (Suica or ICOCA) at the station for seamless transit payments throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Kyoto and head straight to Maruyama Park for the Cherry Blossom Viewing (Hanami) experience. Arrive early (by 9:00 AM) to enjoy the famous weeping cherry tree before crowds build. Spread a picnic mat under the blossoms and enjoy the serene atmosphere with the family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the surrounding Higashiyama district on foot. Walk the historic Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka stone-paved lanes lined with traditional shops and tea houses. Visit Kiyomizudera Temple (¥500 entrance) for stunning city views and cherry blossom scenery from the wooden stage.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely walk back through Maruyama Park at dusk when lanterns illuminate the cherry trees — a magical experience for families. Head to Nishiki Market nearby for affordable dinner bites before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel breakfast (¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Picnic under the cherry blossoms — buy onigiri, sandwiches, and drinks from a convenience store (¥600–¥900 per person)
meals.dinner: Nishiki Market food stalls — try grilled skewers, tofu, and pickles (¥800–¥1,200 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Mid-April is peak cherry blossom season — Maruyama Park's weeping cherry tree is one of Japan's most iconic hanami spots. Arrive early to claim a good spot. Bring a picnic blanket and light jacket as evenings can be cool. Free entry to the park itself.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Arashiyama for the Bamboo Grove experience. Walk through the iconic towering bamboo forest early in the morning (before 9:00 AM) when it's quietest and most atmospheric. The rustling bamboo and filtered morning light make for stunning family photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the bamboo grove, hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park (¥550 adults, ¥250 children). The 20-minute uphill hike rewards you with over 120 wild Japanese macaques and panoramic views of Kyoto. Kids especially love feeding the monkeys through wire mesh. Explore the Togetsukyo Bridge area and the Oi River banks dotted with cherry blossoms.
day_by_day.evening: Take the scenic Sagano Romantic Train (if budget allows, ¥880 per person) or walk back through Arashiyama village. Browse local craft shops for budget souvenirs. Have dinner at a casual ramen or udon shop in Arashiyama before heading back.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery or convenience store near the hotel (¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Arashiyama street food — matcha soft serve, yudofu (tofu hot pot), or packed bento (¥700–¥1,100 per person)
meals.dinner: Ramen or udon shop in Arashiyama — look for set meals under ¥1,000 (¥800–¥1,200 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The bamboo grove is free to enter. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Monkey Park hike — it's a moderate incline but very manageable for families with children. Bring water and snacks. The park closes at 17:00 so plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Fushimi Inari Taisha — the famous shrine with thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up a forested mountain. Entry is completely free and open 24 hours. Hike as far as the family is comfortable — even the first 30 minutes offers spectacular photo opportunities. Cherry blossoms along the lower trails add extra beauty in April.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to the Gion district, Kyoto's historic geisha quarter. Walk Hanamikoji Street and explore the preserved machiya townhouses. Visit the free Yasaka Shrine. If timing is right, you may spot a maiko (apprentice geisha) heading to an appointment in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a budget-friendly kaiseki-style set meal at a local teishoku (set meal) restaurant in Gion. Alternatively, grab affordable sushi at a conveyor belt sushi restaurant (kaiten-zushi) like Kurazushi or Hamazushi where plates start at ¥110.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or local coffee shop breakfast (¥500–¥800)
meals.lunch: Inari sushi (kitsune-zushi) near Fushimi Inari — very fitting and budget-friendly (¥600–¥900)
meals.dinner: Kaiten-zushi conveyor belt sushi restaurant (¥1,000–¥1,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free and one of Japan's most iconic sights. Start early to beat the crowds. The full hike to the summit takes about 2–3 hours round trip but partial hikes are perfectly rewarding. Wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Nara — just 45 minutes from Kyoto by train. Visit Nara Park where over 1,200 free-roaming sika deer bow to visitors in exchange for shika senbei (deer crackers, ¥200/pack). Kids absolutely love this experience. Walk to Todai-ji Temple, home to Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue (¥600 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Kasuga Taisha Shrine (free outer grounds) with its hundreds of stone and bronze lanterns draped in moss. Walk the forested paths between the shrines and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere. Browse Naramachi, the historic merchant district, for affordable crafts and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto or your hotel base by early evening. Have dinner at a local izakaya (Japanese pub) — order shared plates of edamame, karaage chicken, yakitori, and cold drinks for an authentic and affordable family-friendly dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store (¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Nara casual restaurant or food stall — kakigori (shaved ice), mochi, or a bento set (¥700–¥1,100)
meals.dinner: Budget izakaya dinner — shared plates and drinks (¥1,000–¥1,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Nara is extremely family-friendly. Purchase deer crackers only from official vendors. Remind children not to tease the deer as they can headbutt! The JR Pass covers the Nara–Kyoto route. Nara Park and most outer shrine grounds are free.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Osaka — about 15 minutes from Kyoto by shinkansen or 30–40 minutes by regular express. Start at Osaka Castle Park (free park entry, ¥600 for castle museum interior). The castle is surrounded by cherry trees still in late bloom in mid-April, making for beautiful family photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Dotonbori, Osaka's famous entertainment and food district. Walk along the canal, see the iconic Glico Running Man sign, and try Osaka's famous street foods. Visit Den Den Town (Nipponbashi) for affordable anime, manga, and electronics for curious kids.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening in Dotonbori sampling Osaka's legendary food culture. This is the perfect budget food destination — eat your way through the street stalls and standing restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel (¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Osaka Castle Park picnic or nearby convenience store bento (¥600–¥900)
meals.dinner: Dotonbori street food feast — takoyaki (¥600), okonomiyaki (¥800), kushikatsu (¥700), and more per person

day_by_day.notes: Osaka is known as Japan's kitchen — food here is world-class and very affordable. Look for standing-only restaurants (tachigui) for the cheapest prices. The Osaka Amazing Pass may be worth considering if planning multiple attractions.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the free Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine in Osaka — one of Japan's oldest and most important shrines, featuring a distinctive arched bridge and serene grounds. Great for a peaceful morning walk. Alternatively, explore Tennoji Park and the free outer zoo grounds for families with young children.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Shinsaibashi shopping arcade for window shopping and budget finds. Visit the 100-yen shops and Don Quijote discount store for affordable souvenirs. Walk to Amerikamura (American Village) for quirky street fashion and affordable vintage finds.
day_by_day.evening: Take a budget-friendly Osaka bay cruise or simply walk along the Nakanoshima riverside park as the city lights reflect on the water. Have dinner at a local teishoku restaurant for a hearty, affordable set meal.

meals.breakfast: Local kissaten (old-school Japanese coffee shop) morning set — toast, egg, and coffee (¥500–¥800)
meals.lunch: Shinsaibashi area food court or standing sushi bar (¥700–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Teishoku set meal restaurant — rice, miso soup, main dish, and pickles (¥800–¥1,200 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Shinsaibashi is great for budget shopping. Don Quijote (Donki) is open 24 hours and sells everything from snacks to electronics at discount prices — perfect for souvenir shopping. Keep receipts for tax-free shopping (purchases over ¥5,000).

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to Himeji — home to Japan's most spectacular castle, Himeji-jo (White Heron Castle). The castle is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the best-preserved original castles in Japan (¥1,000 entry). Cherry blossom trees in the castle grounds create a breathtaking setting in April.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return toward your hotel base. Stop at a local onsen (hot spring bath) facility for a relaxing family soak — look for a public sento (bathhouse) charging ¥400–¥600 per person. This is a wonderful cultural experience and perfect for tired legs after days of walking.
day_by_day.evening: Low-key evening near the hotel. Visit a local supermarket around closing time (19:00–20:00) when bento boxes and sushi trays are marked down 30–50% — a savvy budget traveler's dinner strategy. Relax and pack for the final day.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel (¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Himeji station ekiben (station bento) — a classic Japanese travel tradition (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: Supermarket discounted bento and side dishes (¥600–¥1,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Himeji is about 30–40 minutes from Osaka by shinkansen (covered by JR Pass). The castle grounds and surrounding Koko-en Garden (¥310 entry) are stunning in cherry blossom season. Start early to avoid peak crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely final morning. Take one last walk through a nearby park or along the waterfront to soak in the atmosphere. Visit a local temple or shrine for a quiet moment of reflection. Buy any last-minute souvenirs at a 100-yen shop or convenience store.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport with plenty of time (aim to arrive 3 hours before international departure). Use remaining yen on airport food, duty-free shopping, or last convenience store snacks. Return any rented pocket WiFi devices at the airport counter.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Carry wonderful memories of cherry blossoms, bamboo groves, friendly deer, incredible food, and rich Japanese culture!

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store final Japanese breakfast (¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Airport food court — try a final bowl of ramen or udon before departure (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Leave extra time for airport check-in and security. Spend remaining coins and small bills at vending machines or convenience stores — coins cannot be exchanged back easily. Take the airport limousine bus or train — cheaper than taxis. Check your IC card balance and consider cashing out remaining balance at station machines.

trip_options.title: Classic Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Narita/Haneda Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. A late-night convenience store stop at a 7-Eleven or Lawson near the hotel is a great way to grab onigiri, instant ramen, or snacks for a light arrival meal.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane
meals.dinner: Late-night convenience store (7-Eleven or Lawson) – pick up onigiri, sandwiches, or cup noodles (¥500–¥1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Focus on getting to the hotel safely. Purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless train and bus travel throughout the trip. Exchange some yen at the airport currency counter or use a 7-Bank ATM.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag with a slow morning at the resort. Enjoy the beachfront views and take a short walk along the shore to acclimate. Head to a nearby local café for a Japanese-style breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local neighborhood around the resort. Visit a nearby shrine or temple for a gentle cultural introduction. Browse local shops and pick up any essentials. If energy allows, take a short scenic walk or ride to a nearby park to see if late cherry blossoms are still blooming in the area.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at a mid-range izakaya (Japanese pub-style restaurant) near the resort. Order a variety of small dishes like yakitori, edamame, karaage, and miso soup to sample Japanese flavors in a casual family-friendly setting.

meals.breakfast: Local café near the resort – Japanese morning set with toast, egg, and miso soup (¥600–¥900)
meals.lunch: Convenience store or casual ramen shop near the hotel (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: Neighborhood izakaya – shared plates and rice dishes (¥2,000–¥3,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag is real – don't over-schedule today. Try to stay awake until at least 9 PM local time to reset your body clock. April 16 may still have cherry blossoms depending on the region, so keep an eye out!

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Kyoto via Shinkansen (bullet train) if not already based there. Upon arrival, head straight to Maruyama Park for the Cherry Blossom Viewing (Hanami) experience. Arrive early to find a good spot under the famous weeping cherry tree before weekend crowds build up. Bring a picnic blanket and enjoy the blossoms at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: After hanami, walk to the nearby Yasaka Shrine and explore the Gion district on foot. Stroll through the historic streets of Hanamikoji, where you may spot maiko (apprentice geisha) heading to appointments. Browse traditional craft shops and souvenir stores.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Gion at a mid-range kaiseki-style set menu restaurant or a casual tofu cuisine restaurant, which is a Kyoto specialty. Return to the hotel or a Kyoto-area accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a bakery near the resort/station (¥700–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Maruyama Park – grab bento boxes from a nearby konbini or local deli (¥1,000–¥1,500 per person)
meals.dinner: Gion area restaurant – Kyoto-style obanzai cuisine or tofu kaiseki set menu (¥2,500–¥4,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Cherry blossoms in Kyoto typically peak in late March to early April, but mid-April can still offer late-blooming varieties. Maruyama Park is especially magical in the evening when the weeping cherry tree is illuminated. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Arashiyama for the Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park experience. Arrive early (before 9 AM) to walk through the iconic towering bamboo forest with fewer crowds. The morning light filtering through the bamboo is stunning for family photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park to see Japanese macaques up close – a huge hit with kids and adults alike. Afterward, explore the Arashiyama riverside area, rent a rowboat on the Oi River, or visit Tenryu-ji Temple and its beautiful garden (UNESCO World Heritage Site).
day_by_day.evening: Return toward central Kyoto or your accommodation area. Have dinner at a casual restaurant near Kyoto Station or in the Shijo-Kawaramachi area. Try a family-friendly shabu-shabu or sukiyaki hot pot restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab onigiri and drinks from a convenience store before heading out (¥500–¥800)
meals.lunch: Arashiyama area café or noodle shop – try soba or udon with seasonal toppings (¥1,200–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Shabu-shabu or sukiyaki restaurant near Kyoto Station – all-you-can-eat sets available (¥2,500–¥3,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Monkey Park entrance fee is around ¥550 for adults and ¥250 for children. Bring cash as some smaller vendors in Arashiyama may not accept cards. The hike to the Monkey Park is moderate – about 20 minutes uphill, but manageable for families.

day_by_day.morning: Participate in the Traditional Tea Ceremony and Kimono Experience in Kyoto. Dress your family in beautiful kimonos and walk through the historic streets of Higashiyama or Gion before the ceremony begins. The tea ceremony itself is a calm, meditative cultural experience that offers insight into Japanese aesthetics and hospitality (wabi-sabi).
day_by_day.afternoon: While still in kimono (if the rental allows extended time), explore Ninen-zaka and Sannen-zaka – charming stone-paved lanes lined with traditional shops, pottery, and sweets. Visit Kiyomizudera Temple for panoramic views over Kyoto.
day_by_day.evening: Return kimonos and freshen up. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in the Higashiyama area. Try a local yakitori restaurant or a cozy ramen shop to wind down after a culturally rich day.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a traditional Japanese breakfast set at a local café (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a teahouse or café near Kiyomizudera – matcha sweets and light bento (¥1,200–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Higashiyama area yakitori or ramen restaurant (¥1,800–¥2,800 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the kimono and tea ceremony experience in advance as slots fill up quickly, especially on weekdays in spring. Many packages include professional photos. Kiyomizudera charges a small entry fee (around ¥500). The stone lanes can be slippery – wear or bring flat shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Kyoto to Tokyo via Shinkansen (approximately 2 hours 15 minutes on the Nozomi). Check into a mid-range hotel in Tokyo (Shinjuku, Asakusa, or Shibuya recommended for families). Drop off luggage and head out to explore the Asakusa district – visit Senso-ji Temple, Tokyo's oldest and most iconic temple, and stroll through the Nakamise shopping street for traditional snacks and souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Asakusa. Visit the Sumida Park nearby to catch any remaining cherry blossoms along the riverbank. Take a short cruise on the Sumida River for a scenic view of Tokyo's skyline and the iconic Tokyo Skytree.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Tokyo Skytree observation deck for spectacular panoramic night views of the city. Dinner in the Skytree Town complex or nearby Asakusa – try a tempura restaurant or a family-friendly sushi conveyor belt (kaiten-zushi).

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry or onigiri at Kyoto Station before boarding the Shinkansen (¥500–¥800)
meals.lunch: Asakusa area – try ningyo-yaki (doll-shaped cakes) as a snack and a bowl of ramen or soba nearby (¥1,200–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) near Skytree or Asakusa – fun and affordable for families (¥1,500–¥2,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Reserve Shinkansen tickets in advance using your JR Pass or book at the station. Senso-ji is free to enter. Tokyo Skytree observation deck costs approximately ¥2,100 for adults and ¥1,050 for children – book online to skip queues.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tsukiji Outer Market for a guided food tour. Explore Japan's most iconic food market and indulge in fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (Japanese rolled omelette), fresh seafood skewers, and street snacks. This is a fantastic sensory and cultural experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market, walk or take a short taxi to the Hamarikyu Gardens – a beautiful traditional Japanese garden with a teahouse on a tidal pond, surrounded by Tokyo's modern skyline. It's a peaceful and photogenic contrast. Afterward, head to the Ginza district for window shopping and a gelato or café break.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Shibuya district. Watch the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing at night – one of the world's busiest pedestrian crossings and a quintessential Tokyo experience. Dinner in Shibuya at a mid-range restaurant – try a teppanyaki grill or a multi-floor izakaya.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market – fresh sushi breakfast, tamagoyaki, and clam miso soup (¥1,500–¥2,500 per person)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Hamarikyu teahouse or a café in Ginza (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Shibuya teppanyaki restaurant or izakaya – grilled meats and seasonal vegetables (¥2,500–¥4,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is best visited early (by 8–9 AM) before the crowds arrive. The inner wholesale market has moved to Toyosu, but the outer market remains open to the public. Hamarikyu Gardens charges a small entry fee (¥300 for adults, free for children under 15).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum (located in Odaiba or the new Azabudai Hills location). This world-class interactive digital art experience is a must for families – immersive rooms of light, sound, and motion create a magical, ever-changing environment that children and adults both love. Book the first entry slot to avoid long waits.
day_by_day.afternoon: After TeamLab, explore the surrounding area. If at Odaiba, visit the Odaiba Seaside Park for a waterfront walk with views of the Rainbow Bridge and a replica Statue of Liberty. Visit DiverCity Tokyo Plaza for shopping and the life-sized Gundam statue (free to view). If at Azabudai Hills, explore the modern architecture and art installations.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Roppongi or Akihabara district for dinner. Roppongi offers a range of international and Japanese restaurants, while Akihabara is great for families interested in anime, gaming, and electronics. Try a themed café or a multi-course Japanese dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near the hotel (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Restaurant inside or near TeamLab – Japanese café-style lunch (¥1,500–¥2,200)
meals.dinner: Roppongi or Akihabara mid-range restaurant – try a Japanese curry house or a family izakaya (¥2,000–¥3,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: TeamLab Borderless tickets must be booked online in advance – they sell out weeks ahead, especially during spring. Tickets are approximately ¥3,200 for adults and ¥1,000 for children (ages 4–12). Allow 2–3 hours minimum inside the museum.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning in Harajuku and Meiji Shrine. Start with a peaceful walk through the forested path to Meiji Jingu Shrine – a serene Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji, surrounded by 70,000 trees. A wonderful cultural and natural experience that contrasts beautifully with Tokyo's urban energy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita Street in Harajuku for quirky fashion, crepes, and pop culture. Then head to the nearby Omotesando boulevard for upscale boutiques and stunning architecture. Visit the Omotesando Hills shopping complex or browse the side streets for independent shops and cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shinjuku for your final full evening in Tokyo. Visit the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck for panoramic city views. Explore the neon-lit Kabukicho entertainment district (family-friendly outer areas) and Golden Gai for atmosphere. Enjoy a farewell dinner at a mid-range teppanyaki or tempura restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast (¥800–¥1,200) or a bakery café near the hotel
meals.lunch: Harajuku crêpe and snacks on Takeshita Street, plus a café stop on Omotesando (¥1,200–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Shinjuku mid-range tempura or teppanyaki restaurant – course meal for the family (¥3,000–¥5,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is free to enter. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is free and open until 10:30 PM (closed some Tuesdays). Harajuku is particularly lively on weekends but still fun on Fridays. This is a great day for last-minute souvenir shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final relaxed morning in Tokyo. Take a leisurely stroll through Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden – one of Japan's most beautiful parks and a top spot for late-blooming cherry blossoms (Shinjuku Gyoen often has varieties that bloom later than Maruyama Park). Perfect for a peaceful family picnic or a final hanami moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel to check out and collect luggage. Do any last-minute shopping at a Don Quijote (discount variety store) or a department store basement food hall (depachika) to pick up Japanese snacks, sweets, and gifts to bring home. Head to the airport with ample time before your departure flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Tokyo. Enjoy a final meal at the airport – Narita and Haneda both have excellent dining options including sushi, ramen, and tonkatsu. Reflect on an incredible 10 days in Japan!

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a final Japanese breakfast set at a café near the hotel (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Shinjuku Gyoen – grab bento boxes from a nearby convenience store or deli (¥1,000–¥1,500 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant at Narita or Haneda – sushi, ramen, or tonkatsu set meal (¥1,500–¥2,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen entry is ¥500 for adults and ¥250 for children. It is closed on Mondays. Allow at least 3 hours to get to the airport from central Tokyo (Narita) or 1.5 hours (Haneda). Use your remaining Suica card balance for train fare to the airport. You can refund unused Suica balance at the airport before departing.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Join locals for picnics beneath thousands of blooming sakura trees, enjoy street food stalls selling yakitori and dango, and soak in the festive atmosphere. The park is especially magical when lanterns illuminate the blossoms at night.

experiences.name: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse your family in a world-class interactive digital art experience where light, sound, and motion blend into breathtaking installations. Children and adults alike are captivated by the ever-changing projections and interactive exhibits. This is one of Japan's most unique and memorable family-friendly cultural attractions.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Japan's most iconic food market and indulge in fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (Japanese omelette), grilled scallops, and matcha treats. Walk through bustling stalls with your family, interact with vendors, and taste your way through authentic Japanese street food culture. A guided tour can enhance the experience with historical and culinary context.

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the iconic towering bamboo forest in Arashiyama, then hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids will love feeding the monkeys from inside a viewing hut while enjoying panoramic views of Kyoto. Combine with a rickshaw ride through the scenic riverside area for a full cultural and nature experience.

experiences.name: Traditional Tea Ceremony and Kimono Experience
experiences.description: Dress your family in beautiful traditional kimonos and participate in an authentic Japanese tea ceremony led by a tea master. Learn the art of matcha preparation, the philosophy of wabi-sabi, and the etiquette of Japanese hospitality. Many studios in Higashiyama offer family-friendly sessions followed by a stroll through historic stone-paved streets lined with cherry blossoms.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival day — no morning activities scheduled. Flight UA arrives at 22:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrival day — no afternoon activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for landing.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, enjoy a welcome amenity (sake or matcha), and settle into your beachfront suite. Light room service available.

meals.breakfast: On board or at airport lounge
meals.lunch: On board or at airport lounge
meals.dinner: In-room dining at Aegean Bliss Resort — request the chef's late-night selection of sashimi, miso soup, and seasonal Japanese sides

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm late check-in with resort. Avoid heavy meals late at night to adjust to the time zone. Keep the first evening relaxed to combat jet lag.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start at the resort. Enjoy a premium Japanese breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant featuring tamagoyaki, grilled fish, rice, miso soup, and seasonal pickles. Take a gentle stroll along the beachfront to acclimate and enjoy the fresh air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area surrounding the resort. Visit a nearby Shinto shrine or coastal garden for a gentle cultural introduction. Hire a private guide to provide historical and cultural context. Stop at a local artisan shop for handcrafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a private welcome kaiseki dinner at the resort's signature restaurant. Kaiseki is a multi-course traditional Japanese meal showcasing seasonal ingredients, exquisite presentation, and refined culinary artistry — the perfect luxury introduction to Japanese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Resort oceanfront restaurant — full traditional Japanese breakfast set
meals.lunch: Light bento lunch at a nearby premium café or resort poolside dining
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant — reserve in advance and request a private dining room for the family

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 2 relaxed to recover from jet lag. Avoid overpacking the schedule. Sunscreen and light layers recommended for beach and shrine exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Depart by private luxury vehicle to Kyoto (arrange early departure). Begin with the Traditional Tea Ceremony and Kimono Experience — dress the entire family in beautiful hand-selected kimonos and participate in an authentic Japanese tea ceremony led by a certified tea master in a historic machiya townhouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Still dressed in kimonos, walk to Maruyama Park for the Cherry Blossom Viewing (hanami) experience. Admire Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in full bloom. Enjoy a private picnic-style hanami lunch arranged under the blossoms with premium bento boxes, sake for adults, and matcha for children.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the atmospheric Gion district at dusk — the lantern-lit streets and preserved wooden machiya create a magical setting. Dine at a renowned Gion kaiseki restaurant. Return to resort by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — Japanese or Western set
meals.lunch: Premium private hanami picnic bento in Maruyama Park — pre-arranged with a local caterer
meals.dinner: Kikunoi Honten or Mizai in Gion — award-winning kaiseki restaurants (reserve weeks in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Book kimono rental and tea ceremony well in advance — premium providers fill up quickly during cherry blossom season. April is peak season; Maruyama Park will be busy but magical. Comfortable walking shoes under kimonos are recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to Arashiyama. Walk through the iconic Arashiyama Bamboo Grove in the early morning before crowds arrive — the towering bamboo columns and filtered light create an otherworldly atmosphere. Your private guide will share the history and ecology of this UNESCO-recognized landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park in Arashiyama — a family favorite where Japanese macaques roam freely with sweeping views of Kyoto below. Afterward, take a private rickshaw ride through Arashiyama's scenic lanes and visit Tenryu-ji Temple's stunning Zen garden, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Enjoy a relaxing evening with a private onsen (hot spring bath) session at the resort's premium spa facilities. Optional: family-friendly cooking class at the resort to learn to make mochi or sushi rolls.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Shoraian — a renowned tofu cuisine restaurant set beside the Oi River in Arashiyama, surrounded by nature
meals.dinner: Resort dinner — request the chef's seasonal tasting menu with local seafood and Kyoto vegetables

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the Bamboo Grove by 7:30–8:00 AM for the best light and fewest crowds. Monkey Park involves a moderate uphill hike — wear comfortable shoes. Children must be supervised around the monkeys.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Tokyo (Shinkansen bullet train from Kyoto Station — book Green Car/Gran Class seats for a premium experience). Arrive in Tokyo and check into a luxury day-use suite or lounge at a partner hotel near TeamLab. Freshen up and prepare for the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum — an immersive, world-class interactive digital art experience where light, sound, and motion blend seamlessly. This is a highlight for families, with children and adults equally captivated by the boundless, ever-changing digital installations. Book premium timed-entry tickets in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the upscale Azabudai Hills or Roppongi area near TeamLab. Explore the illuminated Tokyo skyline from a rooftop bar before returning to the resort by private transfer or overnight Shinkansen.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before Shinkansen departure
meals.lunch: Bento boxes in Gran Class on the Shinkansen — a quintessential Japanese travel experience
meals.dinner: Dinner at Azabudai Hills — try Sézanne (French-Japanese fusion, Michelin-starred) or a premium sushi omakase counter in Roppongi

day_by_day.notes: Book TeamLab Borderless tickets months in advance — they sell out quickly, especially during cherry blossom season. Gran Class Shinkansen seats include meal and drink service. Consider a same-day return to the resort or book a luxury Tokyo hotel for one night.

day_by_day.morning: If staying overnight in Tokyo: Begin with the Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour. Arrive early (by 8:00 AM) to experience the market at its most vibrant. Indulge in fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, matcha soft-serve, and seasonal street foods with a knowledgeable private guide who curates the best stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Ginza district for premium shopping — visit flagship stores, traditional craft shops, and Japanese department stores (depachika basement food halls are a must). Optional: visit the Mori Art Museum in Roppongi Hills for contemporary Japanese art.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Tokyo with a sky-high dinner at a Michelin-starred restaurant with panoramic city views. Return to resort by private luxury transfer or Shinkansen.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market food tour — fresh uni, otoro sushi, tamagoyaki, and green tea
meals.lunch: Depachika premium bento or lunch at a Ginza restaurant — try Kyubey for legendary Edomae sushi
meals.dinner: Dinner at Signature (Mandarin Oriental Tokyo) or Joël Robuchon Tokyo for a world-class fine dining experience with Tokyo skyline views

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji is best visited early morning. Wear comfortable shoes for the market. Ginza stores open around 11:00 AM. Confirm return transfer timing to ensure smooth travel back to the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Resort recovery day. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely premium breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning at the resort's private beach or pool. Optional: sunrise yoga or meditation session on the beachfront arranged by the resort concierge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a private cultural workshop at the resort or nearby — options include ikebana (Japanese flower arranging), sumi-e (ink painting), or origami with a local master artisan. This is a wonderful family bonding activity that produces beautiful take-home keepsakes.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset cruise along the coastline arranged by the resort — enjoy champagne, seasonal canapés, and the golden hour over the water. Return for a relaxed resort dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — Japanese set with seasonal fish, tofu, and pickles
meals.lunch: Resort poolside lunch — fresh seafood, sashimi platters, and cold noodles
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant — request an omakase-style dinner showcasing the chef's best seasonal creations

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest day to recharge mid-trip. The private sunset cruise should be booked through the resort concierge at least 48 hours in advance. Ikebana and art workshops are ideal for all ages.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided day trip to Nara. Visit Nara Park where hundreds of free-roaming sacred deer bow to visitors for shika senbei (deer crackers) — a beloved family experience. Explore the towering Todai-ji Temple housing Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue, a breathtaking UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Naramachi, Nara's beautifully preserved merchant district. Visit a premium lacquerware or Nara ink shop for authentic artisan souvenirs. Explore Kasuga Taisha Grand Shrine, lined with thousands of stone and bronze lanterns draped in moss.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Indulge in a full luxury spa evening — private onsen, shiatsu massage, and a rejuvenating facial treatment. Light dinner at the resort's wellness café featuring healing broths, seasonal vegetables, and premium Japanese whisky or sake.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Edosan inside the Nara Hotel — a historic grand hotel serving refined Japanese cuisine in an elegant Meiji-era setting
meals.dinner: Light wellness dinner at the resort spa café — seasonal miso soup, steamed vegetables, grilled fish, and matcha dessert

day_by_day.notes: Purchase deer crackers from official vendors only. Deer are gentle but can be persistent — keep food out of sight when not feeding. Todai-ji is impressive but crowded; arrive early. Nara is a comfortable day trip from most resort locations.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided exploration of a local fishing village or traditional coastal town near the resort. Meet local fishermen, learn about traditional Japanese fishing culture, and participate in a morning fishing excursion on a private boat. Bring your catch back to the resort for a custom-prepared lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby historical castle or samurai district for a deep cultural immersion. Hire a private guide in samurai armor for a family photo experience and sword demonstration (iaido). Explore the castle grounds and surrounding cherry blossom trees still in late bloom.
day_by_day.evening: Host a private family dinner on the resort's beachfront terrace — a bespoke multi-course meal designed by the resort's head chef, featuring the morning's fresh catch alongside premium wagyu, seasonal vegetables, and artisanal Japanese sake pairings. Stargazing on the beach afterward.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before the fishing excursion
meals.lunch: Resort kitchen prepares your morning catch — grilled, sashimi-style, or in miso soup, served with rice and pickles
meals.dinner: Private beachfront bespoke dinner — wagyu, fresh seafood, seasonal kaiseki courses, sake and whisky pairing

day_by_day.notes: Coordinate the fishing excursion and catch-to-table lunch with the resort concierge at least 3 days in advance. The private beachfront dinner is the trip's signature luxury moment — request florals, lanterns, and live koto music for a truly unforgettable setting.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the resort. Wake up early for a last sunrise walk along the beach. Enjoy a premium farewell breakfast with the family — reflect on the journey over fresh pastries, seasonal fruit, Japanese coffee, and matcha. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time: visit a final local highlight — a serene Japanese garden, a coastal shrine, or a premium pottery studio for a last artisan memento. Resort concierge arranges final gift wrapping of any purchased souvenirs and coordinates luggage handling.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to the airport. Arrive with ample time to enjoy the premium airport lounge — Japan's airport lounges (particularly ANA Suite Lounge or JAL Sakura Lounge) offer exceptional food, sake, and relaxation before departure. Board flight home with beautiful memories of Japan.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — full Japanese and Western spread with fresh juice, seasonal fruit, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or en route — onigiri, soba noodles, or a premium bento for the road
meals.dinner: Premium airport lounge dining or in-flight first-class meal service

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport procedures. Request the resort concierge to prepare a farewell gift bag — often includes local teas, sweets, and a handwritten note. Confirm all souvenirs comply with customs regulations (no fresh food items). Leave a review and tip for your private guide and resort staff.
